description: Single source of truth for AutoFlow's per-phase spawn policy (model + effort). Read it with scripts/spawn-policy/spawn-policy.sh; never restate its values in prose (docs/core.md > Spawn Model — Phase-by-Phase).
sample_contract: This file is a SAMPLE carrying the values currently applied, not a universal vocabulary the framework enforces. It is the plugin's default: a target that keeps its own copy at `.claude/autoflow/spawn-policy.json` overrides it, and that copy is the target's to configure. On a version bump, a target with its own copy runs `scripts/spawn-policy/spawn-policy.sh check` and adds any newly required row — PREFLIGHT's target check (`scripts/preflight/target-check.sh`, leg D6) runs that check and the required-row comparison against this default, so a stale copy is reported there with the rows to fix; a workflow that reads a workflow_sites row fails closed on a missing one. `check` reads the agent definitions from the agents/ directory of the AutoFlow root the readout runs from — the root the session loads. A phases[].effort on a shipped definition is not a target-side lever: it must equal the `effort:` frontmatter line of the definition the session loads and `check` fails closed otherwise — see effort_contract.phase_effort_ownership; a target that needs a different direct-spawn effort changes the shipped definition, not this row. A `general-purpose` helper row's effort and workflow_sites effort stay target-configurable.

effort_contract.is_the_vocabulary_check_applies: `scripts/spawn-policy/spawn-policy.sh check` reads its admitted effort vocabulary and its inherit sentinel from THIS object. A runtime with a different effort vocabulary is accommodated by editing this contract, never by patching the checker; model values are not validated beyond presence and shape
effort_contract.admitted_one_spelling_per_level: this policy admits one spelling per level; the harness alias "med" for "medium" is not admitted here
effort_contract.sentinel_is_config_only: "inherit" is this file's own vocabulary and is never written to any harness channel: a Workflow agent() opts object omits the effort key, an agent-definition frontmatter omits the effort line, and an Agent call that spawns a general-purpose helper omits the effort parameter
effort_contract.absent_means: identical to "inherit" — the row declares no override and the spawn inherits the session effort. A row carrying no effort key at all is a validation error, not an inherit: `spawn-policy.sh check` rejects it
effort_contract.phase_effort_ownership: A phases[] row's effort is DELIVERED by the agent definition's `effort:` frontmatter line, not by this file. Phase-row effort is fixed per plugin version and is not a per-target lever; this file's phases[].effort is the projection source at the tool repository and must equal the loaded definition's line — `check` fails closed on a mismatch. Only workflow_sites effort reaches its spawn from this file at run time and is configurable per target. A row that uses a harness research type (Explore / Plan / claude-code-guide) admits the inherit sentinel only; `check` refuses a concrete effort there. A row that uses the harness `general-purpose` type — the helpers a unit spawns — has no definition to carry its effort: the spawn passes the row's effort as the Agent tool's `effort` parameter, or omits the parameter when the row reads out the inherit sentinel, so `check` admits any value in the vocabulary there, does not require such rows to agree with each other, and compares no frontmatter. The projection is recognised in one canonical spelling only — `effort: <value>` at column 0 of the first YAML block, unquoted, no trailing comment; any other spelling a YAML parser could read as that key — including an indented key — is refused by `check`. The block itself is accepted in block style only — one plain `key: value` per line at column 0, blank lines and `#` comments; a flow mapping, an explicit key, a merge key or a multi-line scalar is refused as a shape, before any "no effort line means inherit" verdict.

gate-plan.work_type: rubric, 5 items × 10 points (intent: decision grounds, verification fit, scope, tools, security)

handoff-review-triage.work_type: review aggregation — the review records of a pull request and the reviews the target's side left on it into one comment and its findings file (source and disposition per finding) — + Low-finding impact judgment

unit-analysis.work_type: U2 Analysis unit (DIAGNOSE + GATE:HYPOTHESIS span) as one spawn — goal, artifact contract and verification prescribed, method its own (ADR-0025 D2); model and effort held at the DIAGNOSE rows' values so the migration step's measurement isolates the method change

unit-design.work_type: U3 Design unit (ARCHITECT + GATE:PLAN span) as one spawn — goal, artifact contract and verification prescribed, method its own (ADR-0025 D2); model and effort held at the ARCHITECT design tier, so the migration step's measurement isolates the method change

unit-build.work_type: U4 Build-and-verify unit (DISPATCH..VALIDATE + AUDIT span) as one spawn — goal, artifact contract and verification prescribed, method its own (ADR-0025 D2); model and effort held at the values of the RED / GREEN rows it replaced

unit-build-area.work_type: U4 helper (docs/units/build.md > Dividing the work) — one design area's Red→Green, its tests, lint and commits, in a context of its own; the unit's own implementation work, held at the unit-build row's values

unit-build-verify.work_type: U4 helper (docs/units/build.md > Dividing the work) — verification and integration after the last implementation commit: run record, verification-row checks, observation follow-up, comment check, build report; the unit's own judgment work, held at the unit-build row's values

unit-build-observe.work_type: U4 helper (docs/units/build.md > Dividing the work) — one observation with a tool: run, judge match / mismatch, probe the cause; non-deterministic work, held at the effort the unit's observation helpers already ran at by inheritance

advisor.work_type: first judgment at a decision point, recorded as an advisor-decision ledger entry (ADR-0025 D7) — highest-capability model at the highest effort; the effort is delivered by the definition's effort: line

criterion-trace.work_type: criterion review stage (U1, CRITERION-REVIEW) — stage 2: the reach of each confirmed cause and each required behavior's conflict with the rules in force, assuming no fix, in a context apart from the review session (issue #445); held at the review session's reference model and effort

criterion-in-depth.work_type: criterion review stage (U1, CRITERION-REVIEW) — in-depth analysis of one criterion's screened cases in a context that never saw the review's verdicts (issue #442); held at the review session's reference model and effort

criterion-reconciliation.work_type: criterion review stage (U1, CRITERION-REVIEW) — reconciliation of the review record with the in-depth analyses, settled in the code (issue #442); held at the review session's reference model and effort
